content: 1. After at least five half-lives of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, the dose of ivosidenib should be increased to the recommended dose of 500 mg once daily. Ivosidenib can reduce the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for reduced therapeutic effects of these drugs. 2. Fosamprenavir can increase the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The interaction between fosamprenavir and ixazomib is minor, with no clinically meaningful changes in systemic exposure observed in clinical trials when ixazomib is coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 3. Fosamprenavir can decrease the levels or effects of ketamine by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Dose reduction of ketoconazole may be necessary for patients receiving more than 400 mg daily. 4. Fosamprenavir can increase the levels or effects of lacosamide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. Fosamprenavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Lansoprazole can decrease the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Fosamprenavir can increase the levels or effects of lapatinib, larotrectinib, lefamulin, lemborexant, and lenacapavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 7. Fosamprenavir can increase the levels or effects of levamlodipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to amlodipine, requiring dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 8. Levoketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Dose reduction of ketoconazole may be necessary for patients receiving more than 400 mg daily. 9. Fosamprenavir can increase the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Fosamprenavir can increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 11. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lidocaine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 12. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of linagliptin and liraglutide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been noted. 13. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lofepramine by decreasing metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lomitapide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Lomitapide increases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction when used concomitantly. 15. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and adjust the dose of CYP3A substrates as per product labeling. 16. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lopinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 17. Fosamprenavir increases levels of loratadine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Lorlatinib decreases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lovastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 20. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor is not expected to exceed that of monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. Following this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. 21. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lumateperone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 22. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lurasidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Coadministration of lurasidone and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 24. Fosamprenavir increases levels of lurbinectedin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Fosamprenavir increases levels of macitentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Fosamprenavir increases levels of maprotiline by decreasing metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Fosamprenavir increases levels of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 28. Marijuana increases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Fosamprenavir increases levels of mavacamten by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. Monitor closely. 30. Fosamprenavir increases levels of mavorixafor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects and reduce the mavorixafor daily dose if necessary. 31. Fosamprenavir increases levels of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Fosamprenavir increases levels of mefloquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine due to the potential for increased toxicity. 33. Fosamprenavir increases levels of meperidine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 34. Fosamprenavir increases levels of mestranol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Variable effects on estradiol may occur. Use non-hormonal contraception. 35. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of metformin through mechanisms related to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Fosamprenavir increases levels of methadone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Fosamprenavir increases levels of methylergonovine by decreasing metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 38. Fosamprenavir increases levels of methylprednisolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Methylprednisolone decreases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Metronidazole increases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Miconazole vaginal increases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Fosamprenavir increases levels of midazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Avoid coadministration of midazolam intranasal with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors due to higher systemic exposure, which may prolong sedation. 42. Fosamprenavir increases levels of midostaurin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor midostaurin for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 43. Fosamprenavir and mifepristone both increase levels of each other by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone increases levels of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 44. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of miglitol through mechanisms related to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Fosamprenavir and mipomersen both have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 46. Fosamprenavir increases levels of mirtazapine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
